---
title: "How do I smooth a noisy time series with a moving average?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I smooth a noisy time series with a moving average?

## Steps to decide and solve

Order the observations; confirm the sampling intervals and choose a window; plot both original and smoothed values to preserve context.

## Worked example: Nile

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("Nile")
smoothed <- ru_apply("moving_average", data=d, x="flow",
                     time="year", window=7)
stopifnot(nrow(smoothed)==nrow(d),anyNA(smoothed$smoothed))
```

The seven-observation window smooths annual flow measurements. It can hide brief peaks and introduces missing values at the centered window edges; the smoothed line is not additional observed data.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("moving_average", data=your_data, x="numeric_column", time="date_column", window=7)
```

If measurements arrive at irregular intervals, a seven-observation moving average is not a seven-year moving average.

Use `ru_plan("moving_average")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
